_about: What is printed at the ticked character on each row of the contact sheets (work/char_sheets/sheet_NN.png), read 2026-11-13 from the images before the key was opened. 'printed' is the glyph; 'seen' is how many occurrences on the sheets show it.

K01.note: i with acute: piíta, kariíkuʔ, cíkic, hiítuʔ, pítku, díʔida

K03.note: a raised dot between syllables: tə•rɪ•kə, kɪ•tuu

K04.note: opening single quotation mark before an English gloss

K05.note: i with acute, every time directly after a plain i: rií, siís, kií, pií, tií, hií

K06.note: u with acute, every time directly after a plain u: suú, ruú, kuú, tuú, huú

K07.note: a question mark ending a Skiri question: asku?, kitaa?

K08.note: s with caron, in citations from other languages: neešaá-, tiš, čeeriš, heduška

K09.note: a with acute, in citations: káhtš, anátš, oowátkAt, okáxpa

K10.note: a stem with grave, always a single short vowel: wɪ̀, rɪ̀, kɪ̀. At higher zoom the stem has the hooked foot of the lax i

K11.note: o with acute, in citations: koóRUx, tstoóxuʔ, aapiróx, ištóh

K12.note: a with ogonek (nasal a): hoočąk, hoočągra, hą, mąhą

K14.note: u with grave directly after a plain u: tə•ruù•wə

K15.note: a full stop, one of the three in (ʊt...)

K16.note: lax u (upsilon shape) with grave: sə•kʊ̀•hə

K17.note: i with acute, in citations and Skiri: aahniítuʔ, teehiítuʔ, awíya, kUxíniʔ

K18.note: u with acute: kAhuúnuʔ, WAhúruʔ, napaʔút, teškúNIt

K19.note: straight apostrophe in English: someone's, one's, spirit's

K20.note: a capital-height H with a caron above it, inside a word: upaȞks-. The same word twice. At higher zoom: a capital H with a caron. The word is rihkuupaȞks-tarit in an example sentence

K21.note: schwa with acute: kə́h, ə́•taa, tskə́, rə́•kɪts, ə́s•kʊ

K22.note: a with grave directly after a plain a: rə•raàh•kə

K23.note: a large bullet between example sentences

K24.note: a with acute, every time directly after a plain a: paá, haá, raá, taá, čaá, saá

K25.note: a small raised i: atⁱnátš, tⁱnaakA

K26.note: e with acute, in citations: šaahéʔ, sčéš, šeéNIt, tičeé, čeésuʔ

K27.note: a straight apostrophe inside a Skiri word where a glottal stop is expected: ra'uk, ahwa'ac, sit+a'u, ka'uk

K29.note: glottal stop, drawn small and raised: htataʔuuku, tuuʔut, raaruʔat

K30.note: i with grave directly after a plain i: kɪ•čiì

K31.note: c with caron in a phonetic form: čaát, čə́•čɪk

K32.note: a with ogonek and acute: umą́hą

K33.note: z with caron: wažáže (the same word four times)

K34.note: closing single quotation mark after an English gloss

K36.note: a curly apostrophe at the end of a Skiri-font word: wuhu’ (the same place twice)

K37.note: c with caron in citations: huučíRIt, nehčítA, čis+wi, sčéš

K38.note: lax i, drawn as a stem with no dot: čɪ, wɪ, kɪ, rɪ

K39.note: exclamation mark ending a Skiri command: uksat!, iihac!

K41.note: a with acute in the serif font: taátuʔ, sát, áwiʔu, rákis, paátuʔ, ásku, haátuʔ

K42.note: b, every time in the English abbreviation 'prob.' inside an etymology bracket. Not a Skiri letter

K43.note: d in the English words 'islands' and 'lands' in italic sans. Not a Skiri letter

K44.note: glottal stop, small and raised, in the serif font: -aʔu, -huʔ, -hiriʔ, aátuʔ, iíkuʔ

K45.note: a stem with acute, every time a single short vowel, never after a plain i: kɪ́•tuu, rɪ́h, kɪ́ts, pɪ́•čuu. At higher zoom (work/char_sheets/zoom.png) the stem has the hooked foot of the lax i, which the tense í of K05 does not

K46.note: the null sign in the serif font: (Ø-)

K47.note: glottal stop in a phonetic form: rʊʔ, wi•ʔuʔ

K48.note: i with ogonek, last letter of ppádį (the same word twice)

K50.note: lax u (upsilon shape) with acute, a single short vowel: rʊ́, kʊ́, sʊ́, čʊ́, ʊ́•kə

K51.note: a dash at the edge of a phonetic form, just inside the bracket: [–ruu, –]

K52.note: a question mark set in a third font inside words cited from other languages, where those languages have a glottal stop: k?ygú, dí?ida, sariit?hkat?. At higher zoom it is an ordinary question mark with its dot
